'''Rachel Lindsey Webster''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AO|FAA}} (born 3 July 1951), is an Australian astrophysicist who became the second female professor of physics in Australia. Her main focus areas are [[extragalactic astronomy]] and cosmology; she researches black holes and the first stars of the universe. Webster has a doctoral degree from [[Cambridge University]] and has held postdoctoral positions at the [[University of Toronto]] and [[University of Melbourne]].

==Early life==
Rachel Webster was born in North East [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]]. She began her schooling at Tallangatta Primary School and then moved to [[Melbourne]] at the age of six, where she attended Blackburn South Primary School and later [[Presbyterian Ladies' College, Melbourne|Presbyterian Ladies' College]] in Melbourne.<ref name="Judge">{{Citation | author1=Judge, Astrid | author2=Fitzpatrick, Jane, 1964- | title=Heroes of Australian science | date=2012 | publisher=Macmillan Education | url=http://trove.nla.gov.au/work/172606193 | access-date=23 November 2015 }}</ref> Her father was an engineer and her mother a geography teacher; both encouraged Webster's interest in physics, science and mathematics from a young age. Webster was inspired to pursue astronomy after she attended a lecture at the [[University of Sydney]] in her final year of school. The lecture was on cosmology, presented by [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford|Robert May]], one of Australia's most celebrated scientists.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

==Career==
Webster graduated from [[Monash University]] in Melbourne in 1975 with a degree in astrophysics. However, let down by her experiences in the university,<ref name="First Impressions">{{cite news|last1=Lunn|first1=Stephen|title=First Impressions: Rachel Webster|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/first-impressions-rachel-webster/story-e6frg6n6-1225740402945|access-date=23 November 2015|work=The Australian|date=27 June 2009}}{{dead link|date=October 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Webster found herself within the Victorian Government's Public Works department, where she bought and sold real estate. After four years of success in that work, in her mid twenties Webster realised that she was not being completely fulfilled.<ref name="First Impressions"/> This lead her to write to [[Martin Rees]], the head of astronomy at Cambridge University, who encouraged her to gain a master's degree in physics prior to being enrolled.<ref name="First Impressions"/> Webster completed an [[MSc]] at the University of Sussex in 1980 and, in 1985, completed her [[PhD]] on [[Gravitational Lensing]] and Cosmology at Cambridge University.<ref name="Find expert Award">{{cite web|title=Prof Rachel Webster|url=http://www.findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/display/person14490|website=Find an expert|publisher=University of Melbourne|access-date=15 April 2018|at=Awards}}</ref><ref name="RW Research">{{cite web|title=Prof. Rachel Webster – Research|url=http://www.ph.unimelb.edu.au/~rwebster/website/research.html|publisher=University of Melbourne|access-date=15 April 2018|date=2017}}</ref> She then undertook a postdoctoral position at the University of Toronto focussing on the [[Einstein Cross]], a gravitationally lensed [[quasar]].<ref name="RW Research"/>

In 1992, Webster returned to the University of Melbourne, where she received a grant for research related to the [[Parkes Observatory|Parkes]] Quasar Survey.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aNFh2wBQvBgC&q=Rachel+Webster&pg=PA109|title=Australian Backyard Astronomy|last1=Bhathal|first1=Ragbir|last2=Bhathal|first2=Jenny|date=2006-01-01|publisher=National Library Australia|isbn=9780642276322|language=en}}</ref> She was primarily concerned with how galaxies bend light, known as [[gravitational lensing]]. Today, her research group uses equipment including the [[Australia Telescope Compact Array]], the [[Gemini telescope]]s, the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] and the [[Chandra X-Ray Observatory]].<ref name="Conversation bio">{{cite web|title=Rachel Webster|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/rachel-webster-11000|website=The Conversation|date=4 July 2012 |access-date=23 November 2015}}</ref> Webster is a member of the International Consortium, helping to design a new low-frequency radio telescope, to be installed in Western Australia.<ref name="Find expert">{{cite web|title=Prof Rachel Webster|url=http://www.findanexpert.unimelb.edu.au/display/person14490|website=Find an expert|publisher=University of Melbourne|access-date=23 November 2015|at=Overview}}</ref> Webster's ultimate aim is to identify the first sources of the universe. This information is being uncovered via her studies and detection of reionised hydrogen atoms and the structural analysis of neutral hydrogen clouds. She has also conducted research into quasar emission regions, cosmology, the [[Murchison Widefield Array]] and dark matter.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

Webster has been the chair of the National Committee of Astronomy and co-created a Women in Physics Program, which has helped increase the number of women graduating in physics at the University of Melbourne.<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.abc.net.au/tv/bigideas/stories/2009/07/17/2629220.htm|title = Where Do Big Ideas Come From|date = 17 July 2009|work = ABC|access-date = 23 November 2015}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* 2020 [[Officer of the Order of Australia]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-01/ad2020_media_notes_-_ao.pdf|title=Rachel Lindsey Webster, Media Notes, Officer (AO) in the General Division of The Order of Australia, Australia Day 2020 Honours List|date=26 January 2020|website=The Office of the Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia|page=58|access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref>
* 2017 Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]]
* 2010 [[Victorian Honour Roll of Women]]<ref name="Judge"/>
* 2008 Member of the Royal Society of Victoria 
* 2007 Fellow of the Australian Institute of Physics<ref name="Judge"/>
* 1998 Fellow of the International Astronomical Union<ref name="Judge"/>
* 1997 Inaugural Australian Institute of Physics Women in Physics Lecture<ref>{{cite web|title=Women in Physics Lecturer|url=http://www.aip.org.au/info/?q=content/women-physics-lecturer|access-date=23 November 2015|archive-date=1 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101055239/http://www.aip.org.au/info/?q=content%2Fwomen-physics-lecturer|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 1988 Member of the American Astronomical Society

Webster is also a former President of Academic Board at The University of Melbourne and has been awarded the Robert Ellery Lectureship.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}
